purpose: Human gold labels for Bishop's professional-domain pre-filter (gate 1) and knowledge-base keep (gate 2), on a snapshot whose replay input is uniform across both splits. Replay after any profile, prompt, or threshold change.

why_v1_exists.defect_in_v0: eval/prefilter_v0/items.json froze two different projections of the database. All 57 prefilter_pass items had abstract=null plus an enrichment-generated summary; all 72 prefilter_reject items had a real abstract and no summary. Field presence therefore predicted the original system decision perfectly, and the summary was a post-hoc positive gloss written after the item had already passed.
why_v1_exists.consequence: Any gate-1 replay reading 'abstract else summary' leaks the label, and the metrics computed on v0 were optimistic. Replaying profile v1.0.0 on uniform abstracts scored accuracy 0.736 / precision 0.667 / recall 0.764, against the 0.798 / 0.754 / 0.782 that v0 reported.
why_v1_exists.fix: replay_abstract holds the canonical arXiv abstract for all 129 items, refetched from the arXiv API. primary_category and categories were captured at the same time. Labels carried over unchanged, keyed by source_id.

gates.question: Given title + replay_abstract only, should this pass the cheap gate?
gates.cost_asymmetry: A false positive costs one enrichment call. A false negative is unrecoverable: rejected entries are never enriched, so they can never re-enter the pipeline. Recall is therefore the protected metric and precision is recovered at gate 2.

gates.question: If this reached the KB, should it hold a first-class indexed slot?
gates.field_naming_warning: This eval set and the calibration/ exports call the score 'enrichment_score'. Production does not. Enrichment Call 2 emits 'relevance_score' (bishop_shared/enrichment_parsers.py), it persists as the entries.relevance_score column, and it reaches the vector-writer as EntryPollRow.relevance_score. The two names denote the same value — arxiv:2606.11375 is 0.35 under both. Use relevance_score when reading code and enrichment_score only when reading these eval artifacts.

reasons.applied_systems: What people or businesses are actually building — products, features, pipelines, ops.
reasons.architecture_tradeoffs: System design, constraints, failure modes, engineering decisions.
reasons.dev_skills: Dev-flow techniques, skills, agent/editor workflows I would reuse.
reasons.rag_retrieval: Retrieval, chunking, rerank, hybrid search, KB design.
reasons.agent_orchestration: Agents as systems: state machines, tools, memory, eval of agents — applied, not GUI-benchmark-only.
reasons.eval_observability: Eval harnesses, tracing, judges, production monitoring, auditing and measurement methodology.
reasons.failure_modes: How LLM or agent systems break: reasoning failures, robustness limits, brittleness, unreliable eval proxies.
reasons.inference_economics: Cost, latency and throughput decisions available at the API boundary: prompt caching, batch APIs, context budgeting, model routing.
reasons.adjacent_stimulus: Off-lane for building, but genuine thinking material — a good read or a seed for a design conversation. Implies pass at tier peripheral.
reasons.adjacent_offlane: Adjacent to the domain but carries nothing I would use. Implies reject.
reasons.base_model_science: The contribution improves the base model or the mathematics of generation: pretraining, training objectives, quantization, compression, decoding algorithms, kernel or KV-cache internals.
reasons.too_academic: Paper-coded experimental, novelty-first, not something I would implement.
reasons.wrong_domain: CV, robotics, market, clinical, hardware, or otherwise off-profile.
reasons.narrow_corpus: Single non-English language, or task-specific modeling in a vertical, without transferable design.

removed.adjacent_interesting: Degenerate in v0: it appeared on 41 reject/drop items and 6 pass items, and was the sole reason on 39 rejects. It recorded a shrug, not a cause. Split into adjacent_stimulus (implies pass/peripheral) and adjacent_offlane (implies reject) so the tag carries the decision.

added.base_model_science: All 14 v0 false positives belonged to this class and the vocab had no home for them, so they were dumped into adjacent_interesting and wrong_domain, hiding the single largest error cluster.
added.failure_modes: The keep-grade false negatives were failure-mode analyses, which v0 could only express as eval_observability or too_academic.
added.narrow_corpus: Separates single-language and vertical-corpus rejections from genuine wrong_domain.
added.inference_economics: Replaces the ambiguous read of inference_serving, which in v0 was applied both to engine internals and to API-boundary concerns.

labeling_rules: Every pass must carry at least one positive reason. In v0, 10 pass items carried only reject-side reasons, which means the vocab was being used to tag topics rather than to justify decisions.
A pass must carry a tier: core if I would build from it, peripheral if it is worth reading but is not a working reference.

Any label whose reasons include adjacent_stimulus, adjacent_offlane, or too_academic requires a written note. These are the hedge classes, and they are exactly where v0's unnoted labels turned out to be unreliable.

Label the two gates independently. In v0 they came out perfectly collinear — pass/keep 47, pass/skim 8, reject/drop 74, with zero crossovers — which made kb_should a restatement of prefilter_should and left gate 2 uncalibratable.
Do not label more than roughly 30 items in one sitting. v0's unnoted tail contradicts its own noted head on the same topic class.

known_defects_carried_from_v0.gate_collinearity: kb_should is currently a deterministic function of prefilter_should, so no gate-2 threshold can be validated against this set. config/index_policy.yaml must stay enforce:false until that is fixed.
known_defects_carried_from_v0.unresolved_enforcement_semantics: When index_policy enforcement is switched on, a drop-band entry currently skips both the store writes and POST /entries/indexed, so it is re-polled and re-skipped every cycle. That is idempotent and never records a false INDEXED state, but it logs forever. The alternative — posting indexed to retire the entry — would claim an item was indexed when it was not. Decide this deliberately before flipping enforce.
known_defects_carried_from_v0.label_contradictions_on_the_model_improv: RESOLVED by adjudication. The unnoted passes on quantization, KV-cache and decoding (arxiv:2606.09937, arxiv:2606.10820, arxiv:2606.10890) were confirmed as tail errors and flipped to reject, matching the noted rejects (arxiv:2606.13126, arxiv:2606.09927). Context compression was carved out as a deliberate exception.
known_defects_carried_from_v0.rule_the_gate_model_cannot_execute: The object-of-study carve-in — pass a training-method paper when its subject is an agent, tool-use loop, prompt or retrieval system — has now been written twice, and increasingly explicitly, and claude-haiku-4-5 still misapplies it. Under v1.2.0 it rejects arxiv:2606.11119 (agentic RL rollout budgets) and arxiv:2606.11459 (prompt optimization) despite both being named policy passes. Further wording iteration on this rule looks exhausted; the untested lever is a stronger model at gate 1.
known_defects_carried_from_v0.unnoted_tail: 95 of 129 v0 labels carry no note, and the tail shows long runs of identical single-tag rejects.
known_defects_carried_from_v0.calibration_example_leakage: Profile v1.1.x names 9 titles from this set as calibration examples. Replay metrics are reported both over all items and excluding those 9; the excluding number is the honest one.

acceptance_for_replay.pre_registered_bar: Against the profile v1.0.0 control replayed on the same replay_abstract inputs and rescored against the adjudicated labels (accuracy 0.674, precision 0.556, recall 0.714, fp 28, fn 14, keep-grade fn 2): a candidate ships only if false positives fall below 12 AND keep-grade false negatives stay at or below 8, measured excluding calibration examples.
acceptance_for_replay.bar_history: The bar was first set against the pre-adjudication scoring of the same control run (accuracy 0.736, fp 21, keep-grade fn 6). Adjudication corrected 12 of 31 labels, which moved the control to fp 28 / keep-grade fn 2 without re-running it. The thresholds were not moved to fit a result — both v1.1.1 and v1.2.0 clear the original numbers too.

results.1.1.0: fp 3, keep-grade fn 23 pre-adjudication. Rejected: recall collapsed to 0.455 because the blanket model-improvement exclusion over-fired on 16 items.
results.1.1.1: acc 0.853, prec 0.917, rec 0.673, fp 3, fn 16, keep-grade fn 4, only 7 peripheral assignments. Clears the bar but leans precision and barely uses the tier.
results.1.2.0: acc 0.833, prec 0.805, rec 0.733, fp 8, fn 12, keep-grade fn 5, 15 peripheral assignments at 0.909 tier agreement. Clears the bar and is the recall-leaning choice with a functioning tier.

acceptance_for_replay.rationale: A candidate that trades recall for precision is not an improvement, because gate-1 rejection is terminal.
acceptance_for_replay.blocked_on: The adjudication queue at eval/prefilter_v1/adjudication_queue.json must be resolved before a recall regression is treated as a real model error.

replay_protocol.input: item.title + item.replay_abstract, uniform across both splits
replay_protocol.control: Replay the previous profile version on the identical input field in the same session. The frozen system.prefilter_decision is NOT a valid control — it was produced on different input text.

do_not: Do not edit items.json after freeze — a new snapshot is a new eval_id
Do not replay on a field that exists for only one split
Do not use the enrichment-generated summary as gate-1 input; it is written after the pass decision
Do not change the profile and claim this set still measures the previous version
Do not treat enrichment_score as the pre-filter gold — they are different gates
Do not report replay accuracy without also reporting the excluding-calibration-examples figure
Do not add open-text reason tags; use reasons[] from the closed vocab
